summary: Initial check-in: data.json is still unseeded (no clients/prospects/todos, default goals only) and no other agent has logged activity yet. Nothing to cross-check yet — will review again once real data and agent activity appear.

Bump Digital/Plumbline), 6 revenue entries, 10 expense entries, 16 prospects (all stalled at follow_up since Aug 17-19), 30 todos, 5 time entries. Folded a full summary into Bump Digital's client Context field in data.json (agency contact, Plumbline brand/competitors, current vs proposed Meta spend, LinkedIn launch plan, management hours, FY27 media budget). Kelsey shared Plumbline's full Brand Guidelines V02 (283pp) directly in chat. Added brand purpose/mission/values, logo/monogram usage, typography (Material Serif + RM Neue), tone-of-voice examples, colour palette hex codes (Ripple Blue/Moss/Sand/Clay + pairing rule), and imagery style guidance into Bump Digital's Context field in data.json — most relevant for Design and Email Campaigns when producing Plumbline creative. Also confirmed the six agent persona files are now committed to the repo at .claude/agents/, so every agent reliably reads this shared context per its own instructions.

Imported Kelsey's spreadsheet of 100 top fitness creators/apps (Kayla Itsines, Whitney Simmons, Jeff Nippard, etc.) into data.json as new prospects in the 'Prospects' stage, with IG handle/niche/followers/region/contact route in each note. Skipped 2 that were already tracked further along (Alexia Clark, Krissy Cela/Evolve You — both already in follow_up). Now at 114 total prospects. Waiting on Kelsey's offer/experience angle before drafting personalized IG DM + email templates for outreach.

Drafted a new fitness challenge email sequence for a client's fall 8-week program, adapted from their past challenge's structure but updated for flat pricing (no price-tier urgency) and a new leaderboard feature. Saved to Google Drive for review; nothing sent or built in Klaviyo yet.

Built a set of 5 Canva graphics (hero announcement, prizes, new leaderboard concept, pre-registration urgency, and rules/how-it-works) for a fitness client's fall 8-week challenge, matching the brand's established visual style. Drafts are ready in Canva for client review before anything is published.
Drafted an end-of-challenge two-email sequence for a client fitness challenge, adapted from a prior challenge template with updated dates and prize structure, saved as a new Google Doc for review.

Kelsey set a new house style rule: never use em dashes in documents/emails/ad copy going forward, use hyphens instead. Added as a standing _styleNote in data.json for all agents to follow, and flagged it to the email-campaigns agent currently revising the October challenge email doc.

Revised the fall challenge email draft per client feedback: confirmed a pre-reg discount code, expanded one email into a full explainer of the new leaderboard/points feature, and applied the new no-em-dash house style. Also corrected the send dates and swapped the feedback-form link in a client's end-of-challenge email draft. Both saved as updated Google Docs for review; nothing sent or built in Klaviyo.

Added a client entry for a fitness coach client to data.json with recurring-challenge context, and recorded a standing rule from Kelsey: a 'free gear for anyone who finishes' giveaway mechanic is discontinued and should be checked for and removed from any past or future challenge messaging/ad copy/emails.

Removed the discontinued 'free gear for finishing' giveaway line from a client's end-of-challenge email draft; checked the other active challenge email draft for the same client and confirmed it never included that mechanic. Updated doc saved for review; nothing sent or built in Klaviyo.

Kelsey requested a new hidden sales landing page for her own wardrobe-designer lead-gen tool at thryvegrowth.com/wardrobe. Gathered requirements (hero copy, page sections, embed-the-live-tool decision, placeholder photos/booking link, no reviews for v1) and briefed the website agent to build it, checking which Drive build of the tool is current before embedding.

Kelsey wants to duplicate the wardrobe tool/page/outreach playbook for the outdoor/landscape design market. Gathered requirements (target market, tool categories, URL slug, outreach list yes/no) and saved the full plan to data.json's ideas list so it survives a context reset. Holding off launching the build until the wardrobe page agent's report lands, to avoid conflicting work on the same tool codebase.
Built a hidden landing page on the agency site for a new lead-gen tool being sold to a niche B2B vertical, opened as a PR for review before it goes live.

Checked the new landing page PR (open, clean merge, no CI configured, no reviews yet - waiting on Kelsey). Scheduled a check-in in an hour. Updated the outdoor/landscape project plan in data.json with the concrete repo/architecture facts and a hosting blocker (no Vercel/API key deployed yet) that will affect that build too.
Wired the real booking link and live demo URL into the hidden lead-gen landing page, and fixed a leftover placeholder-brand name in the demo tool's AI chat prompt.

Kelsey merged the hidden lead-gen landing page PR - it's now live at its hidden URL. Flagged that the embedded demo tool itself still needs one manual end-to-end run-through (upload/render/chat/lead form), since the build session couldn't reach the hosting provider to verify it, and that the branding fix to the demo tool needs confirming it actually redeployed.

Discovered the merged landing page PR was missing a fix from a follow-up commit that never made it into the merge - the live page had a blank demo embed and a placeholder contact link instead of the real ones. Reapplied that fix in a new PR, along with Kelsey's requested layout changes (new section headline, a vertical step-by-step layout with descriptions trimmed, single-image gallery cards instead of paired ones, and several more call-to-action buttons). New PR open for review, not yet merged.

Kelsey confirmed she'll reuse the existing AI billing key for the new outdoor/landscape lead-gen tool and handle hosting herself. Built the tool (forked and reskinned from the wardrobe one, correctly branded from the start) and sent it to her directly as a file, since this session's GitHub access can't create new repositories. Saved a full status update to data.json so the remaining work (the landing page copy, outreach list) can pick up cleanly later.

Added reference/headline-formulas.md (the 200+ headline formula library) to the repo as a shared reference doc any agent can use for headlines/subject lines/hooks.
